Körber takes a stake in NAiSE for mixed-fleet orchestration

The partnership deepens warehouse fleet integration while NAiSE remains independent and open to other manufacturers.

PR Newswire ↗22 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryVideos 1

An existing collaboration becomes an investment

Körber announced a stake in NAiSE on October 22 to expand intralogistics fleet-management software. Founded in 2017, NAiSE had been self-funded. The deal deepens an existing collaboration, without disclosing investment size or ownership percentage.

A common layer for mixed vehicles

The platform connects AGVs, AMRs from multiple vendors and manually driven industrial trucks through a shared control layer. Integration with WMS, WES and WCS supports coordinated material flow instead of isolated vendor-specific fleets.

Independence and future applications

NAiSE’s founders retain operational management and the company remains open to other integrators and vehicle manufacturers. The partners plan deeper Körber warehouse integration and future humanoid use cases. That roadmap is not an announcement of an operational commercial humanoid fleet.
